correctness.rationale: Two synthetic output rankings formed from ordered unanimous-pair blocks and reversed block order preserve unanimous comparisons twice and orient every cross-block pair once each way. On any three candidates, the probability of at least two unanimous edges is exactly 6·3^-n−6·6^-n, yielding the matching-event union bound. The unanimous-pair indicators have marginal 2^(1-n) and incident-pair joint 2·3^-n+2·6^-n; disjoint index pairs have a valid dependency graph, so the Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon bound vanishes for m~c2^(n/2), giving Poisson(c²). The literal mirror construction works iff no unanimous edge. Independently exhaustively checked all m=3,n=2/3 and m=4,n=2 profiles and exact outputs for matching graphs. The Chen-Stein step, not finite enumeration, establishes the asymptotic law.
residual_risks: The matching criterion is sufficient, not necessary; 3^(n/3) not a claimed sharp general existence threshold.
